course_name_original: Control y Monitorización en Sistemas de Energía Eléctrica Renovable
course_name_en: Control and Monitoring in Renewable Electrical Energy Systems
prerequisites: Students must certify that they have passed basic skills and competences in power electronics, power plants, electric machines and control systems, microcontrollers and automation. This can be either accomplished at his/her incoming student profile and CV or, if not covered there, by passing the related subjects of the first semester.

learning_outcomes.text: Be original in the development and application of ideas, within a research environment.
Solution of problem in new and unfamiliar multidisciplinary environments, related to its knowledge area.
Integration of knowledge, facing the complexity of issuing judgments and sentences parting from some information that includes ethic and social liability constraints.
Ability of communicating justified decisions and conclusions, to specialized and unspecialized listeners.
Use of computers and digital processors in the analysis, design, simulation, monitoring, control and supervision of power systems.
Critical analysis of the information coming from the sensing and instrumentation subsystems.
Practical and experimental verification of monitoring and controlling electrical energy conversion systems, including safety operation of electric systems
Understanding of the importance and the area of utilization of electrical power systems for generation, transmission and distribution of electrical energy
Characterization and modelling of the main energy sources and electric power loads
Ability to understand the basics of the dynamic modelling of electrical power systems.
Characterization, operation and design of electronic topologies and control methods for electric energy conversion
Identification of the main characteristics, design strategies and the constructive elements and materials of the Electrical Power Systems
To know and to compare different power converter topologies applied to both power systems and electric and hybrid vehicles.
To design power converters and control systems for application in wind generation systems, photovoltaic systems and electric traction.
To integrate communications systems in power systems.
To integrate monitoring systems in power systems

syllabus_topics: Operation and control of power conversion for REGS: AD/DC power conversion
Operation and control of power conversion for REGS: DC/AC power conversion
Operation and control of power conversion for REGS: AC/AC power conversion
Operation and control of power converters in Wind Generation Systems (WGS): Principles of control of AC wind generators (IM/DFIM/PMSM)
Operation and control of power converters in Wind Generation Systems (WGS): Control of 3-phase AC/(DC)/AC power converters (partial/full scaled converters)
Operation and control of power converters in Wind Generation Systems (WGS): Grid integration of WGS.
Operation and control of power converters in Photovoltaic Generation Systems (PVGS): Principles of control of Photovoltaic Generation Systems.
Operation and control of power converters in Photovoltaic Generation Systems (PVGS): Parallel operation of PVGS.
Operation and control of power converters in Photovoltaic Generation Systems (PVGS): Grid integration of PVGS.
Monitoring and supervision of power generation systems

assessment_methods.method: Written tests (objective tests, short answer tests and / or test development)
Oral tests (individual, group, presentation of topics/projects, etc.)

assessment_rules: The final student’s qualification is obtained as follows: 30% from proposed works/projects, 10% from proposed simulations, 35% from an individual written test (mandatory, minimum 4/10 score), 15% from oral tests, and 10% from attendance to presential hours (minimum 80% required). For students unable to attend lectures regularly, the 10% for attendance will not apply, and homeworks and exams will be as for regular evaluation with flexible deadlines.
